text:
sam: Heads-up — FP8 kernel enable on L40S is showing a subtle quality drift on AWQ/GPTQ quantized variants when running long-context (8k+) workloads. Seen across canary A/B and a couple Dedicated stacks.

maria: Can you paste an example? Is it a correctness regression or perf?

sam: Mostly accuracy deltas (coherence drop / hallucination increase) after ~3000 tokens; perf numbers look fine. Attn outputs look noisy. Short runs <1k tokens ok.

devin: This smells like a KV cache scaling / activation range mismatch when switching from FP16 path to FP8 kernels mid-run. We saw something similar with a tiled GEMM tweak last year.

alexa: Logs: attaching truncated dump — kernel prints show different scale factors applied at layer 18 for batch 3.

sam: ```
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] kernel: tile(18) scale=1.23e-2
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] kernel: matmul_fp8_v2 run_id=canary-03 seq=3210
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] cache: kv_write seq=3210 size=121MB
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] attn: out_shift=+1 overflow=false
```

ross: Are the canaries mixing H100 vs L40S nodes? Different kernels can have different rounding behavior.

sam: Yes — the rollout target group included both H100 and L40S to validate autoscaling. Only L40S side showed the drift.

maria: Quant deltas: AWQ 4-bit had a +3.8 BERTScore drop on our summarization eval at 8k context; GPTQ 4/8-bit had +2.1 drop. FP8 mixed-precision baseline (ours) had +4.1. Numbers are averaged over 50 prompts.

devin: Hmm. That magnitude suggests a per-layer activation scaling mismatch rather than catastrophic NaNs. Could be tiling handshake where the last tile applies a different exponents bias.

alexa: I ran a quick bisect: disabling dynamic activation scaling for layers 16-20 removes the regression on L40S. So it's likely interaction between dynamic-scaler and FP8 kernel tiling.

sam: Proposed mitigations: 1) Canary rollback for L40S FP8 kernels. 2) Add per-layer fixed scaling thresholds for canary. 3) Short-term: force AWQ/GPTQ workloads to use FP16 fallback on L40S.

ross: For deployment profiles — Hosted users (shared runtime) will hit this when autoscale pools add L40S. Dedicated customers with pinned pools are safe until they switch kernels. Need a config knob in the control plane to disable FP8 kernels per pool.

devin: Agreed. Also add an automated eval in the canary pipeline that runs 10 long-context prompts and checks token-level divergence after 2k tokens. Fail if BLEU/BERTScore drop >1.5.

maria: Can we push a hotfix to the FP8 kernel to use the same exponent clamp as H100? If the diff is small we can hotpatch and re-canarize.

alexa: I have a small kernel diff that forces exponent alignment and avoids dynamic rescale between tiles. Running perf smoke now.

infra-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout paused for canary-03 (reason: quality regression detected). Ticket: https://redsquad/issues/INF-2345

sam: OK — immediate actions: 
- pause L40S FP8 canary (infra)
- add per-pool FP8 enable flag (platform)
- add long-context regression eval to canary (eng-ml)
- verify alexa's kernel diff on a local L40S testbed (ml-kernel)

maria: I'll draft the canary eval checklist and add metric thresholds.

devin: I'll prep the fallback policy to force FP16 for AWQ/GPTQ on L40S until kernel fix validated.

sam: Thanks. If alexa's hotpatch looks good, let's do a limited re-roll to 5% traffic on L40S with the strict eval gate.

ross: Also notify support + product about possible customer-visible deltas for any apps using long-context summarization in the last 48h.

alexa: Hotpatch finished initial run. Perf delta: +2% latency on per-token but eliminates the accuracy drift in our 50-sample eval. Pushing PR now.

sam: Great. Keep this thread updated with PR/rollout IDs. We'll close when canary passes the divergence check. :thumbsup:
